crosswalks.label: Software Developers
crosswalks.rationale: Software Developers ground implementation, tooling and integration work, but developer-tool engineering is a specialization around tools used by other developers rather than application/product software broadly.

crosswalks.label: Computer Programmers
crosswalks.rationale: Computer Programmers contribute debugging, testing and code/tool interaction evidence relevant to developer workflows while remaining a different occupation boundary.

findings.summary: O*NET software/programming evidence supports tool-building, debugging, testing and code-oriented workflows while no exact occupation isolates the developer-tools specialization.
method_labels: O*NET 31.0 Software Developer and Computer Programmer occupational comparison
findings.rationale: The candidate body narrows the broad software baseline into tooling contracts, diagnostics, transformations and provenance.

findings.summary: Developer-tool output can expose evidence and automate transformations but cannot become correctness authority for the professions that consume it.
method_labels: Occupational workflow comparison plus AXM tool/authority review
findings.rationale: A reusable tool layer becomes dangerous if its convenience silently replaces the professional judgment it was built to support.

gaps_against_body.description: Make tool-output authority explicit: tools may transform, test, generate and diagnose, but their outputs cannot silently become target-profession correctness or shared-state authority.

nonclaims: This packet does not claim complete reconstruction of Developer Tools Engineer.
Software Developer and Computer Programmer mappings remain partial/adjacent rather than AXM profession identity.
No target-software correctness, TEST, WORKING, CANON or consuming-profession authority is created.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: This packet grants no target-profession, security, operations, shared-state or institutional authority.
